  • Method Details

    • price

      U price()
      Retrieves the price of the shop.
      Returns:
      the price of the shop as an instance of type U, where U represents a generic type.

    • price

      void price(U price)
      Sets the price for a shop.
      Parameters:
      price - the price to set for the shop; must be of type U and should not be null

    • format

      @NotNull @NotNull String format(@NotNull @NotNull String world, @Nullable @Nullable String currency)
      Formats a string representation based on the provided world and optional currency.
      Parameters:
      world - the name of the world for which the string is being formatted; must not be null
      currency - the optional currency to include in the formatted string; can be null
      Returns:
      a formatted string combining the world and currency information; never null

    • format

      @NotNull @NotNull String format(@NotNull @NotNull String world, @Nullable @Nullable String currency, int quantity)
      Formats a string representation based on the provided world, optional currency, and quantity.
      Parameters:
      world - the name of the world for which the string is being formatted; must not be null
      currency - the optional currency to include in the formatted string; can be null
      quantity - the quantity to include in the formatted string; represents a non-negative integer
      Returns:
      a formatted string combining the world, currency, and quantity information; never null

    • priceComparator

      Comparator<U> priceComparator()
      Provides a comparator for comparing instances of the generic type U used in the shop's pricing.
      Returns:
      a Comparator for comparing values of type U

    • comparePrice

      default int comparePrice(U other, boolean reversed)
      Compares the price of the current shop with the price of another shop.
      Parameters:
      other - the other ShopPrice<U> instance to compare with; must not be null
      reversed - whether the comparison should be reversed (i.e., descending order)
      Returns:
      a negative integer, zero, or a positive integer as the price of this shop is less than, equal to, or greater than the price of the other shop

    • getMaxAffordable

      int getMaxAffordable()
      Retrieves the maximum number of items that can currently be purchased or acquired based on the shop's available balance and the price of the items.
      Returns:
      the maximum number of items that can be afforded; always a non-negative integer.

    • canAfford

      boolean canAfford(int itemAmount)
      Determines whether the current shop can afford the transaction of a specified quantity of items.
      Parameters:
      itemAmount - the number of items involved in the transaction; must be a non-negative integer
      Returns:
      true if the shop can afford the specified number of items, false otherwise
